title: Mockturtle Ragout (Mock Turtle Ragout)
description: Prepared with calf's head, shallots or onions, and peppercorns.
steps: Set the calf's head and ox palates in cold water with salt on the fire, skim well and cook them with shallots or onions, mace, peppercorns and bay leaves for 2 to 2½ hours until tender and cut them into proper pieces.
Take the calf thymus, cook it, cut it into small pieces and let them with the sausages brown in butter.
Make flour browned in butter, add some beef bouillon drawn with herbs and shallots, stir it until a good smooth and well-bound sauce.

Add lemon slices without pits, fine pepper, a pinch of cayenne pepper, some mace and pimento and cook the meat together with morels, mushrooms and capers, as well as 1½ to 2 tablespoons Liebig's Meat Extract for about a quarter hour and add salt to taste.
When serving, stir in Madeira wine.

description: Prepared with kidney, egg white, and onion.

ingredients.name: 6 to 8 thin slices of casino bread

steps: Soak the kidney several hours in cold water, remove the fat and chop or grind it finely

title: Om eene Ham tot Roken in te Zouten (To Salt a Ham for Smoking)
description: Prepared with ham, salt, and saltpeter.

ingredients.name: optional: coarsely ground cloves, pepper, Jamaica pepper, bay leaves

steps: Meat must lie for at least 24 hours and be completely cooled before cutting
Rub each piece individually with salt and saltpeter carefully, calculating one pound salt and one and a half loot saltpeter for 16 pounds meat
Lay the pieces close together in a sturdy oak barrel with the bottom strewn with mixed salt
Sprinkle salt and saltpeter between each layer and arrange so salt comes on top and the specified amount is distributed evenly
For a more piquant taste, mix coarsely ground cloves, pepper and Jamaica pepper with the salt to rub in, and strew some bay leaves between each layer
When the barrel is well filled, seal it properly and turn it daily a few times on its bottom
Large pieces such as hams must lie four weeks before they are well penetrated with brine; smaller pieces such as tongues are ready in three weeks
For the ham, make an incision underneath at the large bone and put salt there so no spoilage occurs at the bone
When the barrel is opened and you want part of the meat to remain, place a wooden lid with a stone on top, turn the meat daily and baste it with its brine

title: Polonaise (Layered Almond Meringue)
description: Prepared with egg whites, almonds, and whipped cream.

ingredients.name: 2 1/2 dl whipped cream with powdered sugar and vanilla pulp

steps: Beat 3 egg whites as stiff as possible, mix them with half of the sifted sugar and pipe from this through a piping bag with a smooth nozzle onto a greased and flour-dusted baking sheet, on which with a lid or bowl 4 circles are marked, 3 rings.
Pipe the 4th circle, starting in the middle, completely full, to serve as the base of the polonaise.
Let the egg white in a very lukewarm oven dry (1 1/2 to 2 hours), but see to it that it remains white in color.
Then beat the remaining egg white stiff, mix it with the remaining sugar and pipe a ring of it on the edge of the base.
Lay a hard ring on it, pipe another soft ring on it and continue thus until the last dried ring is laid on it.

Now spread the outside and inside of the polonaise as smoothly as possible with the remaining egg white, sprinkle the outside with snippered, light brown toasted almonds and let the polonaise in a very lukewarm oven become dry and crisp (1 1/2 to 2 hours), but see to it that it remains as light as possible in color.
Fill it with whipped cream, mixed with powdered sugar and vanilla pulp or with ice.

title: Rijstpudding met Abrikozen (Rice Pudding with Apricots)
description: A pudding made with rice, apricots, and vanilla or sugar.

ingredients.name: 16 g white gelatin or 14 g powdered gelatin
1 small can apricots or 200 g apricots cooked in the usual way

steps: Cook rice porridge in the usual way with the vanilla (recipe 577).
Mix it, just before the rice is done, with the sugar, but make sure the rice grains are not ground fine.
Soak the leaf gelatin 10 to 15 minutes in cold water, then dissolve it in the rice porridge removed from heat.
Let the mixture cool.
Remove the vanilla.
Beat the cream and egg whites stiff.
Add the rice porridge to it and let this mixture stand, stirring occasionally, until it becomes gelatinous and the rice grains no longer sink.
Drain the apricots, layer them alternately with the rice porridge in a mold rinsed with unbeaten egg white, but make sure the first and last layer consists of rice porridge.
Let the pudding become cold and stiff, turn it out onto a damp dish and serve with apricot sauce.
Use the apricot liquid in the sauce.

Place the mixture in small molds rinsed with unbeaten egg white or water and let the mixture cool.

title: Rissoles (12 pieces)
description: Prepared with butter or margarine, jam or filling, and flour.
steps: Prepare puff pastry in the usual way (recipe 846). Roll it out one last time into a large, thin sheet and cut out circles with a diameter of 8-10 cm. title: Roastbeef (Roast Beef)
description: Prepared with beef fat or butter or margarine, salt, and pepper.

ingredients.name: 150 g beef fat or 200 g butter or margarine

steps: Weigh the meat, wash it and rub it on all sides with salt (and some pepper).

Heat the fat in a roasting pan (or cut fresh fat, after washing it, into small pieces and roast these first). As soon as blue vapor comes from the fat, turn the meat on all sides through it, place the lid on the pan, reduce the heat and roast the meat on top of the stove, turning it occasionally, 15 minutes per 500 g.
Pour some water by the fat as soon as the color becomes too dark and the meat is evenly brown on all sides.
Remove the meat when it has roasted for the specified time. Test by pricking it to see if it is done inside.
Make the fat hot again until blue vapor comes off and a crust forms on the bottom of the pan. Pour in enough water so that the crust can dissolve in it and remove the jus immediately from the heat.

Alternatively: Make the fat so hot in a roasting pan that blue vapor comes off. Roll the weighed, washed and salted meat in it and roast it in a hot oven 10 to 15 minutes per 500 g. Baste it every 7 minutes with the fat during roasting. Pour water by the fat as soon as the meat is brown and the color would become too dark. Finish the jus as indicated above.

title: Rolled Cake (Opgerolde Koek)
description: Prepared with cornstarch, jam or marmalade, and eggs.
steps: Stir the egg yolks with the sugar until it is completely finely ground.
Add the sifted flour.
Beat the egg white stiff and mix it as lightly as possible with the remaining dough.
Spread the dough onto a piece of buttered parchment paper, which is placed on a greased baking sheet and projects a little above all sides.
Let the cake bake in a fairly warm oven until light brown and cooked through (at least 10, at most 15 minutes).
Test if it is cooked by seeing if it easily comes away from the paper.
Meanwhile place a piece of grease-free paper on the table. Sprinkle some sugar on it and turn the cake with the brown side onto it.
Pull off the paper on top and then spread the light side as quickly as possible with some thin jam or marmalade, which if necessary has been warmed slightly.

description: Prepared with herrings, gherkins, and onions.
steps: Soak small herrings for 24 hours in water with some milk, refreshing as needed

Arrange lemon slices, onion slices and Spanish pepper alternately between the fish and the glass

Sew the tripe closed, prick it here and there to prevent bursting and cook the stuffed tripe for 2 hours in plenty of boiling water with salt and a few cloves.

description: A bread preparation made with dough or butter or kidney or fat, filling, and pork.

title: Savarin met vruchten (Savarin with Fruits)
description: Prepared with fruits, yeast, and flour.
steps: Make a fairly slack starter dough from approximately 100 g flour, yeast and some lukewarm milk. Let it rise in a warm place for approximately 20 minutes. Make a dough from the rest of the flour, the eggs, the sugar and possibly the rest of the milk, add the butter in small pieces at a time and knead the dough as for bread dough; then work the risen starter dough into it. Place the dough in a ring mold brushed with butter and sprinkled with breadcrumbs. Let it rise for 1 hour and then bake the savarin for approximately 3/4 hour in a hot oven. Meanwhile prepare the fruits. Catch the fruit juice and add some liqueur to it or dissolve extra sugar in it. Turn out the savarin and prick holes in it with a larding needle. Soak the ring with the sweet and aromatic fruit juice. Let the ring cool, fill it with the fruits and garnish the savarin with fruits and with cream. If the savarin is served hot (and with warm compote) then the cream garnish should be omitted, but if for example a small pitcher of cream is served separately.

title: Schildpadsoep (Turtle Soup) (10-12 servings)
description: Prepared with calf's foot, beef, and onions.

ingredients.name: English sauce and soya or Madeira to taste

steps: Wash the foot and let it cook gently with 1 l water for 1 hour
Cut off the fine pieces of meat to serve later as garnish in the soup
Brown the diced shank meat, chopped onions and carrot in 70 g butter or margarine, taking care that this mixture does not burn
Add a little water if necessary
Put them in a pan, add the calf's foot and 1 l water and let everything infuse together for 3 hours
Strain the bouillon, add 1 l fresh water and let this broth infuse gently for another 3 hours
Strain it, let it cool and skim the fat from the 3 broths
Combine them and let them simmer gently with the herbs for a quarter hour
Melt the butter or margarine, add the flour and bring to a boil while stirring, rub out all lumps and gradually add the strained bouillon
Let the soup simmer while stirring until cooked (10 minutes)
Warm the meat pieces from the foot in it and add English sauce and soya or Madeira away from heat
